description: The VISSR on GMS-5 (Himawari-5), with a split-window and a water-vapour channel. Curves from the EUMETSAT NWP SAF RTTOV SRF collection, which credits the original JMA files.
facility_description: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) geostationary meteorological satellites (GMS / MTSAT / Himawari series).

notes: Spectral response functions of the VISSR on GMS-5 (Himawari-5) (Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)), from the EUMETSAT NWP SAF RTTOV spectral-response-function page rtcoef_gms_5_imager_srf.html (https://nwp-saf.eumetsat.int/site/software/rttov/download/coefficients/spectral-response-functions/); the owner's own file is not available online (see Sources). NWP SAF README: 'This file generated: 15/10/2019 README SRF: README file for GMS 5 VISSR imager filter response Last update March 1st 2017 SRF available at: http://www.data.jma.go.jp/mscweb/en/operation/response/gms5.txt README file for GMS_IMAGER filter response Last update March 25th 2011 GMS-5 SRFs are available at: http://isccp.giss.nasa.gov/response/gms-5i.html Water Vapour channel 3 is corrected according to JM Breon paper in JAOT 1999: NOVEMBER 1999 NOTES AND CORRESPONDENCE 1851 Evidence of Atmospheric Contamination on the Measurement of the Spectral Response of the GMS-5 Water Vapor Channel FRANCOIS-MARIE BREON AND DARREN JACKSON Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences, University of Colorado, Boulder, Colorado JOHN BATES Climate Diagnostic Center, NOAA/ERL, Boulder, Colorado ABSTRACT The GMS-5 geostationary satellite carries a channel centered at 6.7 mm for the measurement o'. Converted from wavenumber (cm-1) to wavelength (Angstrom, lambda = 1e8/sigma) and sorted; negative samples set to 0; scaled to peak 1. DetectorType=energy is assumed: the owner gives a normalised (relative) spectral response
